correctness.rationale: For 0<a<1/2, g_a(x)=x/(1+x^2)^a is odd strictly increasing and concave on positive halfline, so any nonfixed two-cycle of F(x)=x-eta g_a(x) must be {R,-R} with R=sqrt((eta/2)^(1/a)-1). Its period multiplier (1-2e_R)^2 is strictly below 1, e_R=(1+(1-2a)R^2)/(1+R^2). For H(r)=|F(r)| and 0<=r<=R, H=h(r)=eta*g_a(r)-r is concave with h(0)=0,h(R)=R. Its range remains <=R iff h'(R)>=0, yielding a<=1/4 or eta<=eta_c(a)=2(4a/(4a-1))^a. Then amplitudes inside (0,R) strictly increase to R, and those outside descend or cross inside. At critical eta, h'(R)=0 forces eventual crossing below R and Taylor coefficient B_a=(5a-1)sqrt(4a-1)/(4a)>0 in R-H(R+delta)=B_a delta^2+O(delta^3), yielding R-H^2(R+delta)=B_a^3 delta^4+O(delta^5). Finite-hit exceptions are countable. Independent symbolic second-derivative and high-precision critical coefficient checks corroborated the algebra.
